items.stem: Explain why d/dx(x² sin x) is not equal to 2x cos x.
items.answer: x² sin x is a product, so the product rule is needed: 2x sin x + x² cos x. Multiplying the separate derivatives is not valid.
items.markingKey: B1 product needs product rule; B1 correct derivative 2x sin x + x² cos x [2]

items.stem: Show, using the quotient rule, that the derivative of tan x = sin x/cos x is sec²x.
items.answer: (cos x cos x − sin x(−sin x))/cos²x = (cos²x + sin²x)/cos²x = 1/cos²x = sec²x.
items.markingKey: M1 quotient rule correctly applied; A1 uses cos²x + sin²x = 1 [2]

items.stem: Aisha differentiates y = (5x + 7)/(2x + 7) using the quotient rule and obtains dy/dx = −21/(2x + 7)². Explain the error and give the correct derivative.
items.answer: The numerator should be v du/dx − u dv/dx = 5(2x + 7) − 2(5x + 7) = 21; Aisha subtracted in the wrong order. dy/dx = 21/(2x + 7)².
items.markingKey: B1 order of subtraction v du/dx − u dv/dx; B1 21/(2x + 7)² [2]

items.stem: Ana differentiates y = (x + 5)/(3x + 4) using the quotient rule and obtains dy/dx = 11/(3x + 4)². Explain the error and give the correct derivative.

items.markingKey: B1 order of subtraction v du/dx − u dv/dx; B1 −11/(3x + 4)² [2]

items.stem: Mohammed differentiates y = x²e³ˣ and writes dy/dx = 2x × 3e³ˣ = 6xe³ˣ. Explain the error and find the correct derivative.

items.markingKey: B1 product rule required; B1 dy/dx = xe³ˣ(3x + 2) [2]

items.stem: Jonas finds the gradient of y = sin x at x = 30° by evaluating cos 30° = 0.866. Explain why this is not the gradient when x is measured in degrees, and state the correct gradient.
items.answer: d/dx(sin x) = cos x only when x is in radians. In degrees, sin x° = sin(πx/180), so the gradient is (π/180) cos 30° = 0.0151.
items.markingKey: B1 result valid only in radians; B1 gradient (π/180) cos 30° = 0.0151 [2]

items.stem: Leila writes d/dx(cos(4x − 6)) = −sin(4x − 6). Explain the error and write down the correct derivative.

items.stem: Nadia writes d/dx(ln(8x + 3)) = 1/(8x + 3). Explain the error and correct it.

items.markingKey: B1 multiply by derivative of inner function; B1 8/(8x + 3) [2]

items.stem: Jonas writes d/dx(ln(7x − 7)) = 1/(7x − 7). Explain the error and correct it.

items.markingKey: B1 dy/dx = (dy/dt) ÷ (dx/dt); B1 1.00 [2]

items.stem: Differentiate y = x ln x with respect to x.
items.markingKey: Product rule: dy/dx = ln x + 1.

items.stem: Kwame differentiates y = (4x + 4)/(4x − 2) using the quotient rule and obtains dy/dx = 24/(4x − 2)². Explain the error and give the correct derivative.
items.answer: The numerator should be v du/dx − u dv/dx = 4(4x − 2) − 4(4x + 4) = −24; Kwame subtracted in the wrong order. dy/dx = −24/(4x − 2)².
items.markingKey: B1 order of subtraction v du/dx − u dv/dx; B1 −24/(4x − 2)² [2]

items.stem: Chloe differentiates y = (6x + 5)/(3x + 1) using the quotient rule and obtains dy/dx = 9/(3x + 1)². Explain the error and give the correct derivative.
items.answer: The numerator should be v du/dx − u dv/dx = 6(3x + 1) − 3(6x + 5) = −9; Chloe subtracted in the wrong order. dy/dx = −9/(3x + 1)².
items.markingKey: B1 order of subtraction v du/dx − u dv/dx; B1 −9/(3x + 1)² [2]

items.stem: What is the derivative of e^(5x)?
items.markingKey: Chain rule: multiply by 5.

items.stem: Hana writes d/dx(ln(9x + 9)) = 1/(9x + 9). Explain the error and correct it.
items.answer: By the chain rule d/dx ln(u) = u′/u, and u′ = 9. Correct: 9/(9x + 9).
items.markingKey: B1 multiply by derivative of inner function; B1 9/(9x + 9) [2]
